correctness.rationale: The Bochner integral of shifted L² profiles has the exact lag-autocorrelation norm formula; differentiation proves F′>0 and F′′<0 under strict K decay. The Q derivative numerator decreases from h to -2M0 and has one root. The implicit overhead comparison is strictly positive; small-lag and finite-moment expansions give the two asymptotic constants. Gaussian F and F′ agree with independent integral and 225 auxiliary numerical checks; the computation is not the global proof.

originality.rationale: On examined full texts and actual mathematical searches, the new object is the infinite-cycle white-noise matched-filter information rate for a translating spectral line. The exact strictly decreasing-autocorrelation uniqueness theorem and the dual short/long overhead powers were not asserted or implied by inspected numerical high-resolution exoplanet cadence, light-curve Fisher information, radio spectral matching, or deconvolved-image capture models. Elementary concavity identities themselves are not claimed to be new; historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: Exhaustive priority against older time-integration, optical signal-processing and motion-blur theory is not established; general quotient/concavity calculus is classical.
The physical objective excludes camera read noise, a finite number of transit exposures and postprocessing; field-specific detection maxima need not match.

value.rationale: The exposure-smearing trade-off is an explicitly motivated unresolved analytic design subproblem of numerical high-resolution exoplanet spectroscopy. The theorem gives an exact global optimum for every positive overhead, an unambiguous Gaussian root and two physically different scaling regimes (cube root and square root). This benchmark clarifies how reducing detector downtime competes with resolving a drifting line and provides a precise baseline for future read-noise and finite-transit analyses. It is not presented as empirical observational guidance.
